work_title: Life is Beautiful (La vita è bella)

places.name: Arezzo
places.connection: Many of the film's outdoor scenes, including the opening scenes, were shot in the historic center of Arezzo.

places.name: Piazza Grande
places.connection: The Piazza Grande is featured prominently in the film, including the scene where Guido rides a horse through the square.

places.name: Teatro Signorelli
places.connection: The theater scenes were filmed at Teatro Signorelli in Cortona.

places.name: Villa Masini
places.connection: The villa used as the home of Dora's family is Villa Masini in Montevarchi.

places.name: Borgo di Castiglion Fiorentino
places.connection: Some scenes were filmed in the medieval town of Castiglion Fiorentino.

places.name: Piazza Grande
places.connection: Numerous key scenes including Guido riding his bicycle, the Fascist parade, Dora's school children marching, and the final 'tank' reveal for Giosuè.

places.name: Caffè dei Costanti
places.connection: Exterior shots of the cafe where Guido frequently waits for Dora, and where some cafe scenes take place.

places.name: Teatro Petrarca
places.connection: Exterior and interior scenes where Guido and Dora attend the opera.

places.name: Palazzo della Provincia (Provincial Palace)
places.connection: Exterior shots for Dora's engagement party, which Guido famously crashes.

places.name: Palazzo Albergotti (Exterior of Dora's Grand Hotel)
places.connection: Used for the exterior shots of the Grand Hotel where Dora works and Guido tries to woo her.

places.name: Via dell'Orto (Guido's Bookshop facade)
places.connection: The street where the facade for Guido's bookshop, 'Libreria Antiquaria Giosuè', was set up.

places.name: Road near Cortona (SP34/SP29 junction)
places.connection: The rural road where Guido and Ferruccio's car breaks down, leading to Guido's first encounter with Dora falling from a barn.

places.name: Cinecittà Studios
places.connection: Used for various interior sets, including parts of the hotel, Guido's apartment, and some interior concentration camp scenes.

places.name: Countryside near Papiano (Concentration Camp set)
places.connection: The location where the extensive exterior set for the concentration camp was built.

places.name: Corso Italia
places.connection: Used for general street scenes, establishing shots of the town, and characters' movements.

places.name: Piazza San Francesco (Church of San Francesco)
places.connection: Visible in some background and establishing shots of Arezzo, featuring the notable Church of San Francesco.

places.name: Duomo di Arezzo (Cathedral of Saints Peter and Donatus)
places.connection: Prominently visible in the Arezzo skyline and background shots, adding to the authentic Italian town setting.

places.name: Via Borgunto
places.connection: A picturesque narrow street leading into Piazza Grande, likely used for various pedestrian scenes and to establish the town's atmosphere.

places.name: Stazione di Arezzo (Arezzo Train Station)
places.connection: Likely used for various train station scenes related to arrivals and departures, and as an inspiration for the deportation sequences.
